Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates unilateral hyperlucency of the right hemithorax with diminished vascular markings (vessel paucity) and a smaller right hilum, which are classic features of Swyer–James–MacLeod syndrome. This condition is a post-infectious obliterative bronchiolitis often associated with a history of recurrent lung infections in childhood, fitting the clinical context provided in the option.
